lines.cap: Stay up all night, three nights in a row, and this is what happens to you.
lines.say: Stay up all night, three nights in a row, and this is what happens to you.

lines.cap: After one night, about twenty four hours awake, your reactions are about as slow as someone over the drink-drive limit.
lines.say: After one night, about twenty four hours awake, your reactions are about as slow as someone over the drink-drive limit.

lines.cap: Your brain starts taking tiny naps without asking. Microsleeps. A few seconds, gone.
lines.say: Your brain starts taking tiny naps without asking. Microsleeps. A few seconds, gone.

lines.cap: After two nights, your mood crashes. Memory slips. Simple maths gets hard.
lines.say: After two nights, your mood crashes. Memory slips. Simple maths gets hard.

lines.cap: By the third night, many people start seeing things that aren't there.
lines.say: By the third night, many people start seeing things that aren't there.

lines.cap: In 1964, a seventeen year old named Randy Gardner stayed awake for eleven days. Record-keepers no longer accept attempts. It's too dangerous.
lines.say: In 1964, a seventeen year old named Randy Gardner stayed awake for eleven days. Record-keepers no longer accept attempts. It's too dangerous.

lines.cap: The good news? A few good nights of sleep usually bring you back.
lines.say: The good news? A few good nights of sleep usually bring you back.

lines.cap: So go to bed. General information, not medical advice.
lines.say: So go to bed. General information, not medical advice.
